meta.title: Naukri job assistant: how an application happens

nodes.label: Part 1: company site
nodes.sublabel: research, link by email, you apply

nodes.label: Part 2: ping
nodes.sublabel: up to 4 a day, you send /apply

cards.title: If it is Part 1: company site
items: The digest and the research email show the employer's direct apply link, read from the job data Naukri's page loads
You apply yourself. At 8 PM, or when you send /applied, Telegram asks: Applied, Not applying or Later
Applied is recorded as applied through company website. Not applying, and the 4th Later in a row, are never suggested again

cards.title: If it is Part 2: Naukri Apply through Telegram
items: A Telegram ping lists the jobs that are ready; send /apply from your phone to start (the listener keeps the PC awake 06:00-23:00; a 19:00 reminder if jobs wait)
Nothing is applied without your Yes tap on that job; no reply in 20 minutes means no
Every button belongs to one card, and a tap is answered within seconds: Applying... please wait, or No - skipped
The right resume is set and checked first (a fresh browser if it has to change), then Apply is clicked

cards.title: How the questions work
items: Naukri's data may list seven questions, but its form asks only what it cannot fill from your profile or earlier tries, so you are asked only the question on screen
Choices are taps; a typed answer gets a quick Yes/No before it is sent; answers go in at Naukri's pace
If the form closes while you think, it is reopened and your answer sent; anything unexpected sends nothing and hands the job back with a screenshot saved

cards.title: Rules for both
items: At most 10 jobs a day, all scoring 80 or more; contract and temporary jobs are never listed
The Apply on company site button is never pressed: Naukri marks the job Applied when it is
At most 4 applications per rolling 24 hours; it counts as applied only when Naukri shows Applied
Part 3 of the digest and the Sunday Excel report show where every job stands
